style: Technical, possession-oriented Asian side under Julen Lopetegui that builds patiently and looks to combine through Afif and Almoez Ali in the final third. Compact defensively with experienced AFC core; can lack a physical edge against bigger opponents.
recent_form: Back-to-back AFC Asian Cup winners and qualified through the AFC route. Almoez Ali was the top scorer in Asian qualifying with 12 goals, underlining their attacking reliability.

key_players.name: Akram Afif
key_players.note: Qatar's brightest attacking talent and chief creator; mainstay since their 2022 home debut, playing for Al-Sadd.

key_players.name: Almoez Ali
key_players.note: Qatar's all-time top scorer (60 goals) and top scorer in Asian World Cup qualifying with 12 goals; the focal point up front.

key_players.name: Hassan Al-Haydos
key_players.note: Most-capped player (188 caps) at 35; leader and link man, plays for Al-Sadd.

key_players.name: Boualem Khoukhi
key_players.note: Experienced defensive mainstay who played every minute of the 2022 home World Cup.

key_players.name: Karim Boudiaf
key_players.note: Al-Duhail anchor providing balance and cover in front of the back line.

historical_news: Qualified for the 2026 World Cup via the AFC route, their first World Cup appearance away from home.
Hired Julen Lopetegui to lead the team into the tournament.
Almoez Ali topped Asian World Cup qualifying scoring with 12 goals.
Reigning multiple-time AFC Asian Cup champions bring continuity and tournament pedigree.
Drawn into Group B alongside Canada, Switzerland and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Cautiously hopeful coverage: regional pride in a continued golden era under Lopetegui and faith in Afif and Almoez Ali, tempered by a difficult European-heavy group and questions about competing against stronger sides abroad.
